1:2.text: People are of two types: The one who affirms [the existence] of the Truth [Allāh] and the one who denies Him. So the opening chapter (al-Fātiḥah) comprises an affirmation of the Exalted Creator and a refutation of the one who denies Him by affirming His Lordship—the Exalted—over the worlds
1:2.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H)

2:3.text: Regarding the statement ...and spend out of what We have provided for them...: Allāh the Exalted often combines between [the mention of] prayer (ṣalāḥ) and charity (zakāh) in the Qurʾān because prayer comprises sincerity (ikhlāṣ) to the Deity [Allāh] and charity and spending comprise benevolence (iḥsān) to His servants. Thus, the sign of the servant’s happiness is sincerity to the Deity and striving to benefit the creation. Just as the sign of the servant’s misery is the absence of these two affairs, there being neither sincerity [to the Deity] and nor benevolence [to the creation].
2:3.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

2:21.text: Meaning, single out (waḥḥadū) your Lord in worship. Ibn ʿAbbās—may Allāh be pleased with him—said: “Everything related in the Qurʾān with respect to worship (ʿibādah), then its meaning is tawḥīd [to single out Allāh with worship].
2:21.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

23:14.text: Regarding So blessed by Allāh, the Best of creators: Some people held that this word should be negated from people because ‘creation’ is ascribed to Allāh, the Exalted. Ibn Juraij said: ‘He said the Best of creators because He the Exalted permitted Jesus—peace be upon him—to create’ and some of them were confused by that. [However], the word [creating] is not negated from humanity upon the meaning of manufacturing (الصنع). Rather, this word (creating) is only negated from them with the meaning of inventing (الختراع) and bringing into existence (الإيجاد) from nothing.
23:14.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

23:14.text: Editorial Note: The world creating (الخلق) has numerous meanings and they include: a) manufacturing, producing (الصنع), in the sense of taking raw materials and producing something out of them, b) determining, defining, specifying (التقدير) the shape, form, attributes and qualities of a thing and c) creating out of nothing (الخلق من العدم). In this verse, the plural form “creators” is used ( الْخَالِقِينَ ), because man was created by Allāh from prior material, just as men create things from prior material. So from this angle, the word ‘create’ can be used for men, without that implying that they create from nothing or are equal to Allāh in their powers of creating. The use of the word (خلق) in the language of the Arabs for the first two meanings is well known, and it is said, (رجل خالق), meaning (صانع) “a manufacturer” and (خلق النعل), “He made shoes” and so on.

Mujāhid said: ‘They make (يصنعون) and Allāh too makes (يصنع), but Allāh is the best of makers (الصانعين).’ The most correct of the sayings is the saying of Mujāhid because the Arabs call every maker, manufacturer (صانع) a ‘creator’ (خالق).
23:14.author: Imām al-Ṭabarī (d. 310H)

23:14.text: Muqātil said: ‘The Exalted says that He is better in creation than those who create idols and their likes, those which are unable to move.’ Editorial Note: And in a modern context, those who try to mimic biology to solve problems and find solutions for humanity—[through the biotechnology science of biomimicry]—then they are unable to replicate the like of what Allāh has created, in its beauty, precision and efficiency. Rather they can only mimic and produce what is inferior, even if it serves a purpose among the purposes for them.
23:14.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 741H)

23:14.text: Editorial Note: This is among the verses used by Evangelical Christians to justify their ascription of rubūbiyyah (lordship) and ulūhiyyah (divinity that necessitates worship) to Jesus. Being unable to validate their doctrines through their distorted and abrogated scripture in the course of disputing with Muslims, they have turned to the Islāmic texts, in order to distort and misinterpret them for the same purpose. These Christians seek to confuse uninformed and ignorant Muslims who have not received a sufficient education in Islāmic creed and the Arabic language. The argument here is that Allāh has affirmed multiple creators alongside Himself, hence the Qurʾān affirms multiple deities, and as such, there is nothing wrong in our belief of Jesus being Lord. From the citations presented, one can see through the ignorance and sophistry in this doubt. The Muslim scholars such as Ibn Khuzaymah (d. 311H), Ibn Taymiyyah (d. 728H), Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H) and many others have explained that there are names and attributes common to Allāh and His creatures such as hearing, seeing, inheriting, guiding, creating and so on. However, there are aspects of the meanings of these words that apply only to Allāh’s attributes and likewise the realities of these attributes are unlike those of the creation, which are imperfect and deficient in their nature and scope. This is a firmly established principle of Ahl al-Sunnah—the people of orthodoxy—in the subject of Allāh’s names and attributes. Educated, informed Muslims will but laugh at these poor souls for their foolishness whilst also invoking Allāh to guide them, out of mercy and pity for them.

39:4.text: Then, He, the Exalted, explained that He has no offspring, unlike the claims of the ignorant polytheists with respect to the Angels [that they are His daughters], or the obstinate among the Jews and Christians with respect to Ezrah (9:30:) and Jesus. So He, the Blessed and Exalted said: If Allāh wished to take a son (for Himself), He could have chosen from what He creates whatever He wills (as a son). Meaning, the affair would have been other than what they have claimed (of His having or taking a son or daughters for Himself). And this [i.e. wishing to take a son] is a condition whose occurrence is not necessitated nor permitted. Rather, it is impossible. He only intended to declare them ignorant in what they asserted and claimed, just as He, the Mighty and Majestic said: (21:17:), and also (43:81:). So this is from the angle of [stating] the condition, and it is permitted to attach a condition to what is impossible on account of the objective of the speaker (in doing so). And the Exalted’s saying But Sublime (is He from such a thing). He is Allāh, the One, the Subduer (who is never overcome). Meaning, Exalted, pure and sanctified is He from that He should have a son, for He is the One, the Uniquely One, the Self-Sufficient Master (who is free of needs) whilst everything else is a slave to Him, and needy of Him.
39:4.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

39:4.text: This is a corroboration of what has preceded of the invalidation of the saying of the polytheists that the Angels are daughters of Allāh. [This is due to what] it comprises of the absolute impossibility of Him, the Sublime, having a son. If He wished to take a son, then taking a son in reality, would be impossible, and that would never arise unless He chooses from what He creates whatever He wills (as a son). Meaning, chooses from the generality of His creation whatever He wills to choose, because there is nothing in existence besides Him except that it is His creation. And it is not correct for a creation to be a son of the Creator due to the absence of kinship and likeness between them. Hence, the only thing remaining is that He chooses a servant, as is afforded through the use of expression of al-Iṣtifāʾ (choosing) in place of taking (al-Ittikhādh). So the meaning of the verse is that if He wished to take a son, then something else would have taken place which is not ‘taking a son’ but rather, it would have been choosing one of His creatures (to be named as a son). For this reason, He the Sublime, exalted Himself from ‘taking a son’ in absolute terms, saying Sublime (is He from such a thing), meaning exalted is He from that.
39:4.author: Al-Shawkānī (d. 1250H)

49:12.text: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d 671H) said: It is established in the two Ṣaḥīḥs [of al-Bukhārī and Muslim] from Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: Beware of suspicion for suspicion [that is expressed] is the falsest of speech, and do not seek information (about others), nor spy (upon others), nor bid over one another (leading to price inflation), nor envy one another, nor hate one another, and nor turn your backs on each other [out of enmity]. But be servants of Allāh, brothers. The wording is al-Bukhārī’s. Our scholars have said: Suspicion here (in the ḥadīth) and in the verse is the conjectural suspicion (تهمة). That which is subject to caution and prohibition is the suspicion having no reason to justify it, such as the one who is suspected of a shameful deed or drinking an intoxicant for example, without anything manifesting from him which necessitates that. The evidence that the suspicion (الظن) here is with the meaning of (التهمة) is the Exalted’s saying ( وَلاَ تَجَسَّسُوا ) do not spy. This is because the conjectural suspicion may occur to him and then he desires to seek information on that, investigating it, watching, listening, in order to corroborate the suspicion which occurred to him. So the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) prohibited from that.

Imām al-Qurṭubī (d 671H) said: That which distinguishes suspicions which are to be avoided from others [that can be harboured] is that everything for which a valid sign (indication) or apparent reason is not known, it is unlawful and is obligatory to avoid. This is when the one against whom suspicion is held is one from whom prudence and rectitude are testified for, and trustworthiness is perceived from him outwardly. To have a corrupt suspicion about him and to betray [what is known about him] is unlawful. This differs from the one about whom it is known among the people that engages in the doubtful, and commits vile things in the open.

49:11.text: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H) said (abridged): This verse, according to Ibn ʿAbbās was revealed in relation to Thābit bin Qays who mocked a man for not making space for him to sit in the mosque, close to the Messenger (صلى الله عليه وسلم). According to al-Ḍahhāk, the verse was revealed in relation to Banū Tamīm who were mentioned earlier (49:4). The belittled the poor among the Companions after seeing their ragged condition. Mujāhid said: “It is the rich mocking the poor.” Ibn Zayd said: “Let not the one whose sin Allāh has concealed mock the one whose sin Allāh has exposed, for perhaps making his sin apparent in the world is better for him in the hereafter.” In summary, it is befitting that no one embark upon mocking the one he sees in a ragged condition, or who has some ailment in his body, or who is not skilled in conversation—for perhaps he is more sincere and of more pious a heart than the one who does not have his shortcomings—whereby he falls into oppressing himself by belittling the one whom Allāh has given respect.

Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H) said (abridged): Nor insult one another Al-Ṭabarī said: “(اللمز) Insulting occurs through the hand (by pointing), the eye, the tongue and through indication whereas (الهمز) only occurs with the tongue.” Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid, Qatādah and Saʿīd bin Jubayr said: “Do not revile each other.” Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: “Do not curse each other.” And it has been said: “From the happiness of a man is that he preoccupies himself with his own flaws away from the flaws of others.”

Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H) said: How evil is the label of disobedience after faith, meaning: How evil it is that a man be labelled disbeliever, or fornicator after his Islām and after his repentance, it was said by Ibn Zayd. And it is said that whoever gave his brother an insulting nickname or mocked him, is a sinner (fāsiq).

Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H) said (abridged): …nor call each other with (offensive) nicknames Al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid said: A man would be blamed for his (prior) disbelief after his Islām, with the saying “O Jew” and “O Christian”, so this verse was revealed. Qatādah said: “It is the saying of a man to another, “O sinner”, “O hypocrite.”

49:13.text: The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: Indeed, Allāh does not look at your appearances and possessions, but He look at your hearts and deeds. Ṣaḥīḥ al-Jāmīʿ (no. 1862). He (صلى الله عليه وسلم) also said: Honour is [itself] wealth, and nobility lies in fear [of Allāh]. Ṣaḥīḥ Ibn Mājah (no. 3418). He (صلى الله عليه وسلم) also said: There is no superiority for an Arab over a non-Arab, and nor a non-Arab over an Arab, and nor a white person over a black person and nor a black person over a white person, except through piety. Mankind is from Ādam, and Ādam is from dust. Ṣaḥīḥ, al-Albānī in Sharḥ al-Taḥāwiyyah.

Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H) said: The Exalted informs that He created the sons of Ādam from a single source, foundation and as a single species, all of them, male and female. All of them return back to Ādam and Eve. However, Allāh the Exalted spread forth from them many men and women and separated them into nations and tribes, meaning small and large [groups]. This is so that they can know each other, for if each of them kept to himself, [the objective] of knowing each other would not have been realised, from which there arises mutual support and aid, inheritance and performance of obligations towards relatives. However, Allāh made them nations and tribes so that these and other affairs can be realised, which rest upon acquaintance and meeting of genealogies. But honour (nobility) is through piety, so the most honourable of them in the sight of Allāh is the most pious of them, which is the most abundant of them in obedience and refraining from disobedience, not the one with most relatives and people, and nor the noblest of them in lineage. Allāh the Exalted is all-Knowing, all-Aware, He knows who among them abides by fear of Allāh, openly and inwardly from the one who does not abide by that, openly and inwardly. So he rewards everyone with what he deserves. And within this verse is evidence that knowing lineage is desired legislatively because Allāh made them nations and tribes for that purpose.

49:14.text: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H) said: These bedouins mentionend in the verse were not Hypocrites [outright] but they were Muslims in whose hearts faith had not settled firmly. So they claimed for themselves a station greater than the one they had reached, so they were disciplined for that.

Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H) said: What has been benefited from this noble verse is that faith (Īmān) is more specific than submission (Islām) as is the doctrine of Ahl al-Sunnah wal-Jamāʿah. It is indicated [also] by the ḥadīth of Jibrīl (عليه الصلاة والسلام) when he asked about Islām, then about Īmān, then about Īḥsān. So he moved from the more general, to the specific, to the more specific.

49:15.text: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H) said: Meaning, [those] who believed and thereafter neve doubted and who corroborated that through jihād and righteous actions. It is they who are the truthful in their faith, not those who submitted for fear of deathh and hoping in acquisition [of goods]. When these verses were revealed, the bedouins swore that they are believes inwardly and outwardly, so then Allāh revealed… the verse that follows.

50:1.text: The Exalted swears by the Glorious Qurʾān, meaning that it is vast in meaning, multifaceted [in its approach], of abundant blessings, of plentiful goodness. Majd means vast and great in its descriptions. The most worthy of speech to be described with this is the Qurʾān—that which comprises the sciences [of divinity, the unseen, the hereafter and the likes] of the earlier and later [nations], that which comprises the most complete type of eloquence, and of words which are most laden with meaning. And the most comprehensive and beautiful of meanings. All of this necessitates perfection in following it, haste in complying with it and gratitude to Allāh for the favour [in revealing it to us].
50:1.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

50:1.text: Qāf is from the letters of the alphabet mentioned at the beginning of chapters such as Ṣād, Nūn, Alif Lām Mīm, Ḥā Mīm, Ṭā Sīn and others. It is narrated from some of the Salaf that they said Qāf is a mountain that surrounds the entire Earth and it is called the Mountain of Qāf. And it is as if this is—And Allāh knows best—from the fables of the Children of Israel which some people took from them on the basis of the permissibility of reporting affairs from them which are neither believed or rejected. In my view, this and its likes are from the fabrications of some of their heretics by which they deceive people about the affair of religion, similar to how in this [Islāmic] nation—alongside the lofty status of its scholars, memorisers and leaders—ḥadīths (traditions) have been fabricated against the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم). [If this is the case with this nation] then how about the Children of Israel given the lengthy period of time, the scarcity of critical scholars [of memorisation and transmission] among them, their consumption of intoxicants, their distortion of words from their proper places and their alteration of the Book of Allāh and His Signs. The Legislator only permitted narrating from them in his saying, “Narrate from the Children of Israel, and there is no harm in it”, with respect to what reason allows. As for what is impossible in reason, is judged to be false, and it being a lie is overwhelming, then it is not of this type [that is permitted to narrate]. Ibn Kathīr goes on to say that many of the Salaf and the Khalaf (later ones) cited abundantly from the People of the Book in interpreting the Qurʾān, which they were not in need of doing. And this is one of the angles from which atheists and apostates criticise the Qurʾān today, due to what they find of such narrations being transmitted in the books of Qurʾān commentary.
50:1.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

53:32.text: From Ibn ʿAbbās regarding ( إِلاَّ ٱللَّمَمَ ) save the lesser sins: “Everything that is between the two limits. The prescribed limit in the world and the limit in the hereafter, then the prayer expiates for it and it is ‘the lesser sin’... As for the limit of the world, then it is every sin for which Allāh has obligated a punishment in the world. And as for the limit of the hereafter, then it is every deed whose performance Allāh has sealed with the Hellfire [as mentioned in what He revealed] and the punishment for which has been delayed for the Hereafter.
53:32.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

53:32.text: And the meaning of the verse ( إِلاَّ ٱللَّمَمَ ) save the lesser sins is: Except when he commits a fāḥishah (sin involving desire) once and then repents, and when it occurs and then ends (not returning to it again). This is the saying of Abū Hurayrah, Mujāhid and al-Ḥasan, and it is also the report of ʿAṭāʾ from Ibn ʿAbbās... and some of them said: They are minor sins such as the glance, the winking of the eye (to solicit an encounter), the kiss and whatever is less than actual fornication. This is the saying of Ibn Masʿūd, Abū Hurayrah, Masrūq, al-Shaʿbī, and it is the report of Ṭāwūs from Ibn ʿAbbās.
53:32.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

53:32.text: (They are) those who avoid major sins and immoral deeds. Meaning, those who do what Allāh has commanded them of the obligations, the leaving of which is from the major sins. And who abandon the major prohibitions such as fornication, drinking intoxicants, consuming interest, murder and what is similar to that of the mighty sins. ( إِلاَّ ٱللَّمَمَ ) save the lesser sins, and these are the minor sins upon which a person does not persist. Or those which a servant falls into rarely, every now and then. So falling into these [types of sins] does not remove a person from being among the righteous (al-muḥsinīn). For this, alongside fulfilment of the obligations and abandonment of the prohibitions, enters (a person) under the forgiveness of Allāh which encompasses every single thing. Hence, He said: Indeed, your Lord is of vast forgiveness . Had it not been for His forgiveness, the servants and the lands would have perished. And had it not been for His forbearance the heaven would have fallen upon the earth and not a single creature would have been left upon its surface. For this reason, the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) said: ‘The five prayers, the jumuʿah to the next jumuʿah, and one Ramaḍān to the next Ramaḍān are an expiation for what is (done) in between them (of sins), so long as the major sins are avoided.’
53:32.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

53:44.text: Meaning: He caused death in this life and gave life in the hereafter. And it is said: He caused the fathers to die and gave life to the sons. And it is said: He caused the disbeliever to die [by making him unknown] and gave live to the believer [by making him known].
53:44.author: Al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

53:45.text: That He originated the creation of the two mates [complimentary partners], the male and the female, and made them into spouses [for each other]. This is because the male is the spouse for the female and the female is the spouse for him. Thus, they are two spouses, each of them is a complimentary partner for the other.
53:45.author: Imām al-Tabari (d. 310H)

53:45.text: He explained the two spouses with His statement the male and the female, and this is the name of a category which comprises all living things, both those capable of speech [upon rational thought] and those unable to do so [such as the cattle]. Thus, He is alone in creating them.
53:45.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

53:45.text: What is intended by the two spouses is the male and female from every living thing.
53:45.author: Imām al-Shawkānī (d. 1250H)

54:14.text: Al-Baghawi (d. 516H) said: With our watch, and Muqātil bin Ḥayyān said: ‘With our protection.’ And Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H) said: With our watch and under our guard and protection. . This verse, along with other texts from the Book and Sunnah, affirms the attribute of Eyes for Allāh, and the principle in this respect, as it is with all the attributes of Allāh, is that they are affirmed with negation of any likeness to the creation. His attributes are unlike those of the creation, since His essence is unlike their essences, just in the same way that the attributes of the Jinn—who hear, see and speak—are unlike our attributes beause their essences are unlike ours. So when dissimilarity is comprehensible between two created things then the difference (in the reality of the essence and its attributes) between the Creator and created is even greater Thus, there is absolutely no caution in affirming the attributes Allāh has affirmed for Himself, and those who negate these attributes by claiming iet is anthromorphism (tashbīh, tajsīm), then they are misguided and in opposition to the Qurʾān, Sunnah and the way of the Salaf. It is tashbīh if it is said:”His hearing is like my hearing, His seeing is like my seeing, His hand is like my hand, His face is like my face” and so on, but it is not tashbīh if it is said: “He has hearing, seeing and a Hand and Face, but they are unlike our hearing, seeing, hands and face, because His essence is unlike ours and is uncreated”, and this is what the Salaf were upon.

54:24.text: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H) said: “This speech is from their misguidance and wretchedness for they showed arrogance towards following a messenger among men [calling them to worship Allāh alone] but did not reject that they should be worshippers of tree, stones and pictures.”

54:43.text: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H) said: If they [the Pagan Arabs] are better than them, it is possible for them to be saved from punishment, and they will not be afflicted with what afflicted with those evil ones. But the affair is not like that, for if they are not more evil than them, then they are not better than them [either].

55:1.text: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H) said: Saʿīd bin Jubayr and ʿĀmir al-Shaʿbī said: ( الرَّحْمنُ ) The Most-Merciful, the opening of three chapters, when combined they become a name from the names of Allāh the Exalted: ( ن) ( حم) (الر). So all of these combined become ( الرَّحْمنُ ). Added by: abuiyaad on 30-Oct-23

55:33.text: The people of interpretation differed about His saying if you are able to pass beyond. Some of them said its meaning is that if you are able to pass the boundary regions of the heavens and earth such that you render your Lord incapable of reaching you, then do so. For you will never be able to do so except with authority from your Lord. They said that this statement will be said to them on the Day of Judgement... And others said that its meaning is that if you are able to pass beyond the regions of the heavens and earth [in order to flee death], then pass beyond them to flee death, but death will certainly reach you, and fleeing from it will not help you. Al-Ḍahhāk said: ‘No one will protect them from death and they will die and not be able to flee from it, there is no escape, even if they passed beyond the regions of the heavens and the earth, they will remain under the authority of Allāh, and Allāh will take them by death.’
55:33.author: Imām al-Ṭabarī (d. 310H)

55:33.text: Meaning, when Allāh gathers them on the Day of Judgement, He will inform them of their incapacity and weakness and the perfection of His authority and the execution of His will and power. So He will say—informing them of their incapacity— O company of Jinn and Mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the boundary regions of the heavens and the earth , meaning, [if you are able] to find some actionable way to escape from the dominion and authority of Allāh Then pass [if you can]! You will never pass [them] except with power, authority [from Allāh]. Meaning, you will not escape from it except through strength and authority of your own, alongside perfect power. But how will they have that, whilst they are not even able to control benefit or harm for themselves, and nor death, life or resurrection?! Hence, in that place, no one will speak except with His permission. Nothing will be heard but whispering, and in that place [on that Day], the kings and the subjects, the leaders and those led by them, and the rich and poor will all be equal.
55:33.author: Imām al-Saʿdī (d. 1376H)

55:33.text: O company of Jinn and Mankind, if you are able to pass beyond, meaning, pass through and exit the boundary regions of the heavens and the earth, meaning, from their sides and outer limits then pass [if you can]!. Its meaning is that if you are able to flee from death by escaping from the boundary regions of the heavens and earth, then flee and escape from them. And the meaning is that wherever you are, death will reach yo, just as He, lofty be His mention, said: Wherever you may be, death will reach you (4:78:). And it is said: It will be said to them on the Day of Judgement, ‘If you are able to pass through the boundary regions of the heavens and earth and thereby render your Lord incapable of reaching you, then pass through [if you can]’, then pass [if you can]! You will never pass through except..., meaning, with authority. And it is said, with proof. And ṣulṭān is complete power, authority over an affair. So authority, power, proof, all of it is ṣulṭān. He intends that wherever you turn towards, you remain under my authority and power.
55:33.author: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H)

55:33.text: Meaning: You will not be able to flee from the command and decree of Allāh. Rather, He completely surrounds you and you are not able to remove yourself from His judgement, and nor from the execution of His command with respect to you. Wherever your go, you will be surrounded. And this is on the gathering plain [of the Day of Resurrection]. The Angels will encircle all of the creatures, in seven rows from every side and no one will be able to depart except with authority, meaning with the command of Allāh.
55:33.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

55:33.text: Editorial Note: From (55:31:) and (55:35:), the Qurʾān commentators state that the context of this verse is the Day of Judgement. The heavens and earth will have been altered and transformed (14:48:), and the people will be gathered, after resurrection, on the plain of the transformed earth. It is here where it will be said O company of Jinn and Mankind, if you are able to pass beyond the boundary regions of the heavens and the earth, with the meaning that if you are able to escape, then try to do so, but you will never be able to do so, except with authority and power from Allāh. This being an indication to their complete powerlessness on that day and being encompassed. As for the verse being a proof for “space travel”, then Shaykh ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz bin Bāz (رحمه الله) stated: “As for His saying, the Sublime, in Sūrah al-Raḥmān... then it is not clear evidence for the possibility of ascending to the celestial bodies because the apparent meaning of the verse, from what is before (55:31:) and after it (55:35:), shows that Allāh the Sublime desired to explain the powerlessness of the two parties [of Jinn and Men] from being able to pass through the boundaries of the heavens and earth. Imām Ibn Jarīr al-Ṭabarī (رحمه الله) and others from the scholars of tafsīr have mentioned numerous sayings in explanation of the verse, the best of them are two: The first, that the intent of the verse is the Day of Judgement. That Allāh has explained [in this verse] the inability of [Jinn and Men] to flee from its terrors. Ibn Jarīr gave preference to this view, and mentioned [as evidence] for what led him to choose this view the verse that comes after it (55:35:). The second saying is that the intent behind it is to explain the inability [of the Jinn and Men] to flee from death, because they have no power allowing them to flee from death. And upon these two sayings, the meaning of sulṭān is strength, power (quwwah). And from what we have mentioned, it is clear that there is no proof in this verse for the one who said that it indicates the possibility of ascending to the celestial bodies, and that “knowledge” is meant by the word sulṭān. It also becomes clear that the closest of sayings is that of the one who said that the Day of Judgement is intended by it... As for this world, then no one is able to pass through the boundaries of the constructed heavens, because they are protected by way of their guards and doors, whose mention has already preceded, and Allāh, the Sublime and Exalted, knows best.” Majmūʿ Fatāwā wa Maqālāt (1/254).

58:2.text: The Qurʾān commentators and linguists have said that “ḍhihār” was pre-Islāmic divorce which represented an emphatic, permanent prohibition. I believe that it was a form of divorce among the people of Yathrib and its surrounding areas, due to their frequent mixing with the Jews. I do not believe it was known among the Arabs of Mecca, Tihamah, Najd and others, I have not come across that in their speech. What is apparent is that prior to Islām they used to mingle with the Jews and adopt their customs. The Jews would forbid a man from approaching his wife (for intercourse) from behind, and hence the word “back” (ḍhahr) appears in the formulation to exaggerate the prohibition, which is to say his wife is like his mother [in prohibition in marriage]. Hence, it is a hideous and terrible formulation [to use for the purpose of divorce].
58:2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr (d. 1393H)

59:2.text: Those intended are Banū al-Naḍīr, a tribe of the Jews, who settled the lands of Arabia, along with Banū Qurayḍhah, and the Jews of Khaybar, and all of them are from the offspring of Aaron (عليه السلام). They used to be called the “Cohenites” because they are from Aaron’s offspring, and he was the Israelite “Cohen”, which means the preserver of religious affairs by hand. The reason for their settlement in the lands of the Arabs was that Moses (عليه السلام) sent a faction of their ancestors to fight the Amalekites in the neighbouring Levant (Shām), but they failed to do so, and then Moses died shortly after that. When they learned about Moses’ death, they returned to the Israelites who said to them: “You disobeyed Moses, so do not enter our land.” So they left for the Arabian peninsula and [through the passing of generations] established townships for themselves around Yathrib (Madīnah). They became agriculturists and traders and had built numerous strong fortresses. Among them were people of affluence such as Samuel bin Adiya, Kaʿb bin al-Ashraf, Ibn Abī al-Ḥuqayq. From the core of those Jews were Banū al-Naḍīr, Banū Qurayḍhah and Khaybar. They were described as those who disbelieve because they disbelieved in the messengership of Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) [despite their full knowledge that is the prophet that they were expecting based on the descriptions in their books]. And they were described as the People of Scripture, so that it is not thought that those intended are the Pagans of Mecca or the Pagans in Madīnah. The detail of the story is what is mentioned by the majority of the commentators that when the Muslims migrated to Madīnah, they, Banū al-Naḍīr, came to the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) and made a covenant of peace with him, which stated that they would remain neutral [between him and the Pagans]. This was after the Battle of Badr, when the Muslims defeated the Pagans of Mecca, and they [the Jews of Banū al-Naḍīr] did not expect the Pagans to be defeated. But when the Muslims were later defeated after the Battle of Uḥud, they broke their covenant with the Prophet and made a covenant with the Pagans [allying with them]. As it was the custom of the Jews to ally with the strong and powerful, the leader of Banū al-Naḍīr, Kaʿb bin al-Ashraf, went with forty riders and formed an alliance with the Pagans to help them fight the Muslims. When this [treachery and conspiracy] was revealed by Allāh to the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم), he sent Muḥammad bin Maslamah to kill Kaʿb bin al-Ashraf in his own fortress, and he did so. Further, in another affair, regarding assistance of payment of blood money for two men of the tribe of Banū ʿĀmīr—with which the Jews of Banū al-Naḍīr had an alliance—who had been killed by ʿAmr bin Umayyah al-Ḍamrī, the Jews of Banū al-Naḍīr conspired to treacherously kill the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) when he was going to meet them regarding the affair. But Allāh revealed their intentions to him. So the Muslims went to them in the month of Rabīʿ al-Awwal in 4 AH, and the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) ordered them to leave their homes and go into exile [as punishment for their treachery]. However, they refused and made war cries. ʿAbd Allāh bin Ubayy bin Salūl (a chief hypocrite) found his way to them and told them not to leave, and that if the Muslims fight them, they would support them, and if they are expelled, they would go with them, and that he had 2000 people on his side, along with [the Jews of] Qurayḍhah and their allies from the Arabs, such as Ghaṭfān. So the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم) besieged them and Banū al-Naḍīr waited for ʿAbd Allāh bin Ubayy, Qurayḍhah and Ghaṭfān to come to their aid in repelling the Muslim army. But when they did not come to their aid, Allāh placed terror into their hearts. They then requested a truce with the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وسلم), but he refused and insisted that they leave and go into exile. So they made a condition that they be allowed to carry camel loads of their belongings. They began to destroy their own homes to take whatever they could use of wood and doors, and then left. Some of them went to the Levant (Shām), some of them went to Khaybar, some to the cities of Jericho and Adhraʿāt and a few went to al-Ḥīrah.
59:2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr (d. 1393H)

59:14.text: Imām al-Baghawī (d. 516H) said: They will not fight you, meaning the Jews all together except in fortified cities, meaning, they do not come out openly to fight you directly [man to man], but they fight you while fortifying themselves with cities and walls. Their enmity between themselves (the Jews and the Hypocrites) is severe, meaning, some of them are harsh towards others and their enmity to each other is severe. And it is said: Their enmity between themselves behind the walls and cities is severe, so when they come out to you (to fight), they are the most cowardly of Allāh’s creation. You think they are together, but their hearts are divided, split, at variance. Qatādah said: “The people of falsehood are at variance in their desires, at variance in their testimony, at variance in their actions, but they are united in showing enmity towards the People of Truth.” Mujāhid said: “He intends that the religion of the Hypocrites differs from the religion of the Jews.”

62:1.text: Since the days resemble each other and cannot be distinguished from each other by any attribute, whether inherent to the day itself or abstract in nature, then their differentiation was left only to numerical means. Hence, they made the names of the week to be derived from numbers, such as the second, the third, the fourth [and so on] or by way of events such as the day of Buʿāth (the place near Madīnah of the last encounter between the Aws and the Khazraj tribes prior to Islām) or the day of (the battle of) Badr or the day of Faṭḥ (victory), and from them is the day of Jumuʿah. There are two views regarding this. The first is due to the people gathering on this day for prayer. The second—and which is the correct view—is that it is the day in which the creation was brought together and perfected [through the creation of Ādam] and it is the day on which Allāh will gather together the first and later ones in order to make judgement.
62:1.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H)

62:1.text: Meaning, He is the Master, Owner of the Heavens and Earth who governs them with His rule and judgement and he is the Perfectly Pure, which means the one sanctified of all deficiencies, shortcomings, described with attributes of perfection. [His saying]: the All-Mighty, the All-Wise, its explanation has preceded more than once.
62:1.author: Ibn Kathīr (d. 774H)

65:4.text: This verse relates to divorce and addresses numerous types of women in a divorce situation. They include: a) Women who have reached or passed menopause, b) the women who have never menstruated at all (due to inability to do so from a condition known as primary amenorrhea) and c) girls who have been married off by their fathers on grounds of beneficial interest. Regarding this third situation, it is when a father marries off his daughter whilst she is a minor—below the age of mental and physical maturity—due to some beneficial interest that would otherwise be lost. This situation can be found frequently in the history of nations all across the world and many examples exist among European royalty. Kings and queens married off their daughters at very young ages because a particular person of royalty, of good standing and character, well-to-do and of means was available. If they delayed marrying off their daughter, they would lose this potential husband to someone else’s daughter. Muslims jurists point out that a girl should not be married off until she has reached bulūgh (maturity) and has expressly given her permission, unless a clear beneficial interest in her getting married prior to this would be otherwise lost. Some Muslim jurists such as Shaykh Ibn al-ʿUthaymīn—who give primacy to the condition of permission—state that even if the father marries off his daughter due to a clear beneficial interest, his daughter should be given a choice if she wishes to continue with the marriage when she reaches maturity and is able to give or deny permission. Hence, the marriage would only be consummated if she has given her permission and when the father has allowed cohabitation. After the marriage contract, the time of cohabitation would then be decided by the parents. Keeping in mind that menstruation may not take place until the age of fifteen years or even later, it is possible for the husband and wife to engage in sexual relations prior to her menstruation if her guardian has allowed cohabitation. If the husband decides to divorce his wife, then this is the situation in which this ruling comes to play. A waiting of period of three months is to verify that she has not become pregnant, such that when the divorce is complete, she is free to remarry without there being any possibility of confusion about the real father of any child she bears. As for commencement of sexual relations, then Muslim jurists state the conditions of physical readiness and absence of any harm. The famous Muslim jurist, Imām al-Nawawī, said: “Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī and Abū Ḥanīfah said that it is the ability to engage in intercourse that defines the time when a father allows his daughter to cohabit with her husband. This varies from one person to another and does not have a specific age, and this is what is correct.” Sharḥ Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim (9/206). Thus, a father will decide when his daughter is ready to engage in sexual relations and allow cohabitation. The Muslim jurists also make clear that a marriage contract on its own does not allow sexual relations, but rather it is the principle based on the Prophetic tradition, There is no causing of harm or reciprocating harm. Hence, when there is physical readiness and absence of harm, then sexual relations can take place. And this would be evaluated and decided by the parents. Likewise, the Muslim jurists make clear that all impediments to harmful sexual activity must be absent before cohabitation is allowed, with the Shāfiʿite jurists holding that even if the husband requests cohabitation with the reassurance that he will not engage in sexual activity, the parents are not to release their daughter, even if the husband was known to be trustworthy (thiqah). As for ages of physical and mental maturity then they are not fixed and vary from era to era and place to place. Prior to the 19th century the age-based distinctions of “child”, “youth”, “teen”, “adult” never existed, and girls and boys became women and men at puberty which coincided with full mental maturity due to the socio-economic conditions in past societies. In fact, frequently, boys and girls became fully mentally mature before any signs of puberty appeared. The delayed onset of “adulthood”—a modern invention—and mental maturity is a recent phenomena. For more details refer to this article. Since mental and physical maturity are variables which greatly differ between individuals in one society and also between individuals across many societies and eras, Islām does not specify any age for marriage. Rather, this is left to the customs and norms of each society which vary due to economic, social and cultural factors. In the modern era, with delayed onset of maturity, “marriageable age” has risen. Considering this, the laws of Islām in this regard are based upon actual ground realities and upon the fundamental facts of human nature and are universal for all times and places. What has preceded can be explained further by the following scenarios: — 1. Lets say, in 18th century Europe, or the colonies in 19th century America when marriageable age was much lower, going as low as the age of 7 in some places. that the parents of an 8 year old girl get her married to a 14 year old boy—as they find him to be an ideal partner, from a well-to-do family. However, they do not allow cohabitation. Five years later, when she is 13, and her husband is 19, they allow cohabitation. The girl at this age is physically able to engage in sexual intercourse, even though she has not started menstruation. So the couple enjoy conjugal relations. However, six months into the marriage, the 19 year old husband—for whatever reason—decides to divorce her and end the marriage. If Islāmic law was being followed, there would be a three month waiting period for this young lady before the divorce is complete. — 2. The parents of a 14 year old girl in the US allow her to get married to a 19 year old man—this is currently legal in many states in the US—and they allow cohabitation. The girl has not yet menstruated and will not do so until the age of 16. The couple have sexual relations, however the man decides to divorce due to unhappiness in the marriage. Or it could be possible that for some medical reason, she never menstruates at all, and they remain married for 7 years. Then he decides to divorce her. In both of these two situations, if Islāmic law was being followed, there would have to be a three month waiting period to ensure she was not pregnant. If she was, then the divorce would not be complete until after she delivers. — 3. A 26 year old woman marries a 30 year old man. This woman has never menstruated and a couple of years later, the man decides to divorce her. Her waiting period is also three months. These illustrations make the intent of the law very clear. The verse covers all possibilities in relation to marriage and divorce and accommodates all social circumstances, in all places, in all times. If in two decades time, the European and American nations lower the age of marriage and consent to 12 years of age—with our knowledge that there will be many girls who will not start menstruating until three or more years later— then Islāmic law will accommodate these situations. It is timeless, because it is based on the fundamental facts of human nature and accommodates individual biological variation as well as all socio-economic conditions and scenarios across all cultures of humanity.

And [likewise], those who have not menstruated, this comprises those who have not yet menstruated due to young age and those who have never menstruated at all, and this is present among the women, where some of them die after having never menstruated. [Likewise], those who reach the time of menstruating and the [signs] of maturity, but she has not menstruated.
65:4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Andalūsī (d. 754H)

65:4.text: Women who never menstruate at all (a condition called primary amenorrhea) do exist, though not common. Around 2% of girls do not start menstruation even by the age of 15 years and overall less than 1% of women suffer primary amenorrhea, meaning, they have not had a period. The legislation of Islām is all-inclusive and comprehensive and accommodates such people in the application of laws which are legislated for humanity's beneficial interests.

74:31.text: This is the state of the hearts when truth is presented to them: —A heart that is put to trial by it, with disbelief and wilful denial. —A heart that is increased by it in belief and faith. —A heart that becomes certain about it, whereby the proof is established against it. —And a heart that is confused and blinded by it, not knowing what is intended by it.
74:31.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (751H)

98:4.text: Meaning, of the Jews and Christians. The People of the Book were specified with splitting as opposed to those besides them—even though they both gathered together with the disbelievers [of all types]—because they are presumed to have knowledge. So if they split [alongside knowledge], then those without a book are more worthy of this description. Until after the clear evidence had come to them. Muḥammad (صلى الله عليه وسلم) is intended by this. Meaning, the Qurʾān is in agreement with what they have in their hands with respect to his [the Prophet’s] qualities and descriptions. This is because they were in agreement about his prophethood [prior to it] but when he was ordered to invite them, they rejected his prophethood, and then split among themselves. So some disbelieved out of envy and jealousy, and others believed, as occurs in the Exalted’saying: And they did not become divided until after knowledge had come to them, out of jealous animosity between themselves (42:14:). It is also said that “bayyinah” means the discourse in their books that he is a prophet that will be sent, and that His saying And they did not become divided... is His judgement upon the one from the People of the Book who did not believe after the establishment of the proof.
98:4.author: Imām al-Qurṭubī (d. 671H)

109:2.text: The intent here is to mention the deity that is described as being worthy of worship, rightfully deserving of it. Thus, He brought [the particle] mā (ما) which indicates this meaning. As if it is said: And nor are you worshippers of my deity who is described as being the only deity worthy of worship in truth. And if He had brought the particle man (من), then it would have indicated the essence (dhāt) only [of the one being worshipped, and not His attribute].
109:2.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H)

109:2.text: The particle mā (ما) indicates an attribute (ṣifah) as opposed to [the particle] man (من), for that indicates an entity (ʿayn).
109:2.author: Ibn Taymiyyah (d. 728H)

109:2.text: That everyone who does not believe in what the Messenger described Him with, then in reality, he has not worshipped whatever the Messenger worshipped, from that angle. And then analogise with this...
109:2.author: Ibn Taymiyyah (d. 728H)

113:2.text: The evil mentioned in this verse is attributed to whatever actions are performed by the creation and not to the Exalted Lord's act of creating [the actions of the servants], which is His action. For there is no evil within [His action] from any angle. Evil does not enter into any of His attributes or actions, just as it is not ascribed to His essence, the Blessed and Exalted... And that which He does of justice towards His servants, and punishing the one who deserves punishment among them, it is pure goodness because it is pure justice and wisdom. It is only evil as it relates to them, when such affairs befall them and take place with respect to them, but not in the act [of creating, rewarding or punishing] that is established with Him. And we do not deny that evil exists within that which He creates, for He is the Creator of both good and evil.
113:2.author: Ibn al-Qayyim (d. 751H)
